docs/extensions.md:6:- **pi-durable extensions** give **tools and prompt sections** to every conversation. Their tools can ask questions, which pi-action posts on the issue or pull request. See [pi-durable extensions](#pi-durable-extensions).
docs/extensions.md:8:Both kinds can also give **prompt templates** (`pi.prompts`). See [Prompts](prompts.md#prompt-templates).
docs/extensions.md:69:A [pi-durable](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-durable) extension adds its tools and prompt sections to every conversation: comment mode, `pr_number` runs, and direct prompts. An example is the `pit/durable` extension of [pit](https://github.com/cv/pit):
docs/extensions.md:83:- The function returns a pi-durable `Extension`: `{ name, tools?, sections?, hooks?, wraps?, tasks? }`.
docs/extensions.md:85:- pi-action installs the extensions after its coding tools (read, write, edit, bash). Each extension must have a unique name. Tool names can repeat (see [Override tools and sections](#override-tools-and-sections)).
docs/extensions.md:87:### Override tools and sections
docs/extensions.md:89:An extension can change the tools and prompt sections of pi-action and of other extensions:
docs/extensions.md:91:- **Replace a tool.** A tool with the name of an earlier tool replaces it, as `pi.registerTool` does in pi. For example, an extension with its own `bash` tool replaces the `bash` of pi-action. pi-action writes `pi-durable extension <name> replaces tool bash from coding-tools` to the log.
docs/extensions.md:92:- **Wrap a tool or a section.** `wrapTool(tool, wrapper)` and `wrapSection(key, wrapper)` of pi-durable change a tool or a section, for example its description or its text. `wrapTool("read", (t) => ({ ...t, callers: ["tools"] }))` hides `read` from the model, but other tools can still call it (see [Tools the model sees](#tools-the-model-sees)).
docs/extensions.md:94:The order is: the coding tools of pi-action (`coding-tools`) first, then the extensions in the order of the `extensions` input. pi-durable applies the wraps of all extensions in this order. Thus, the last wrap wins.
docs/extensions.md:137:- pi-action resolves the names against the tools after it installs the extensions, and after the [overrides](#override-tools-and-sections). For a name that matches no tool, pi-action writes a warning.
docs/extensions.md:142:An extension can also hide a tool itself, with a wrap that sets `callers: ["tools"]` (see [Override tools and sections](#override-tools-and-sections)). The inputs apply after the wraps, and they only remove tools. Thus, an input cannot give the model a tool that a wrap hid.
CONTRIBUTING.md:168:2. Open a pull request with the title `chore: release X.Y.Z`. Write the notes in a `## Release notes` section of its description, in the [release notes format](#release-notes).
CONTRIBUTING.md:178:5. `release.yml` makes sure that the tag agrees with `package.json` and is on `main`, and runs `npm run check`. Then it creates a draft GitHub Release with the `## Release notes` section, and moves the major tag (`vN`) to the commit. It does not move the major tag back for a tag that is earlier than the latest one.
76:- **One file has side effects.** [`src/index.ts`](src/index.ts) reads the environment and creates the GitHub client. All other code gets its dependencies as parameters (`ActionDependencies` in [`src/run.ts`](src/run.ts)), so tests can replace them.
85:| [`src/index.ts`](src/index.ts) | Entry point: creates the dependencies and calls `run()` |
86:| [`src/run.ts`](src/run.ts) | Orchestration of a run |
87:| [`src/run-context.ts`](src/run-context.ts) | What a run works on: an event, `pr_number`, or a direct prompt |
88:| [`src/inputs.ts`](src/inputs.ts) | Reads the action inputs into `ActionInputs`, with the defaults for empty or invalid values |
89:| [`src/defaults.ts`](src/defaults.ts) | The default values of the inputs |
90:| [`src/security.ts`](src/security.ts) | The allowlist check (`validatePermissions()`) and `sanitizeInput()` |
91:| [`src/github.ts`](src/github.ts) | `extractTriggerInfo()` for webhook payloads, and the `GitHubClient` interface |
92:| [`src/triggers.ts`](src/triggers.ts) | Finds the `@pi` comments that a thread must answer |
93:| [`src/context.ts`](src/context.ts) | The task, the built-in prompt, templates, and follow-up messages |
94:| [`src/formatting.ts`](src/formatting.ts) | The comments that pi-action posts, and review comments as prompt context |
95:| [`src/thread.ts`](src/thread.ts) | One issue or pull request as a durable pi conversation in git |
96:| [`src/conversation.ts`](src/conversation.ts) | Submits requests, waits within the timeout, and delivers each result one time |
97:| [`src/models.ts`](src/models.ts) | The built-in providers, with the `api_key` input as an in-memory credential |
98:| [`src/custom-provider.ts`](src/custom-provider.ts) | The custom provider from the `provider_*` and `model_*` inputs |
99:| [`src/extensions.ts`](src/extensions.ts) | The `extensions` input: npm installation, entry points, loading with jiti, and the `pi` object |
100:| [`src/extension-provider.ts`](src/extension-provider.ts) | Changes `pi.registerProvider(name, config)` into a pi-ai provider |
101:| [`src/durable-extensions.ts`](src/durable-extensions.ts) | Creates the pi-durable extensions (`pi.durable`) with the host options of the run |
102:| [`src/github-ui.ts`](src/github-ui.ts) | Questions (`ui.ask`) as GitHub comments, and `ui.notify` in the job summary |
103:| [`src/answers.ts`](src/answers.ts) | Answers from the event (a ticked box or an `/answer` reply), checked and changed into a `ui.answer` submission |
104:| [`src/tool-env.ts`](src/tool-env.ts) | `GH_TOKEN` and the `github-actions[bot]` git identity for the tools of the agent |
105:| [`src/push.ts`](src/push.ts) | The `if: always()` step that pushes thread state that the run did not push |
106:| [`src/worktree.ts`](src/worktree.ts) | `WorktreeContinuity`: saves the working tree at turn boundaries, points the conversation at each snapshot (the `pi-action.worktree` document), and restores it at the start of a run |
107:| [`src/storage/git.ts`](src/storage/git.ts) | Git objects in the process, and compare-and-swap ref updates |
108:| [`src/storage/git-storage.ts`](src/storage/git-storage.ts) | `GitStorage`: a pi-durable `Storage` whose log is a chain of commits on one ref |
109:| [`src/storage/sync.ts`](src/storage/sync.ts) | `GitSync`: fetches a thread ref, and pushes it (fast-forward only) at turn boundaries, with its working-tree ref in one atomic push |
110:| [`src/storage/worktree.ts`](src/storage/worktree.ts) | Working-tree snapshots as git stash commits, chained on `refs/pi/worktrees/<n>`, and their restore |
111:| [`src/types.ts`](src/types.ts) | Shared types |
112:| [`src/utils.ts`](src/utils.ts) | Small helpers |
113:| [`src/test-helpers.ts`](src/test-helpers.ts) | Test fixtures: inputs, a fake GitHub client, faux models, and scratch git repositories |
114:| [`src/test-setup.ts`](src/test-setup.ts) | Removes `GIT_*` variables (for example from a git hook) and sets a git identity for the tests |
122:The tests use [Vitest](https://vitest.dev/). They are next to the code (`src/**/*.test.ts`, `scripts/**/*.test.js`).
124:- **No network, real git.** The tests use the faux provider of pi-ai instead of a real model, and a fake GitHub client from [`src/test-helpers.ts`](src/test-helpers.ts). They run git in scratch repositories, with a bare repository as the remote.
128:- **Documentation tests.** [`src/action-docs.test.ts`](src/action-docs.test.ts) and [`src/defaults.test.ts`](src/defaults.test.ts) compare the inputs table in [`README.md`](README.md#inputs) with `action.yml` and `src/defaults.ts`. [`src/docs.test.ts`](src/docs.test.ts) checks the links in all Markdown files, the template variables in [`docs/prompts.md`](docs/prompts.md), and the `extensions:` examples.
